CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: intervertebral disc

2 of 3 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 0 fall below it; 1 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • Glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST; chondroitin/dermatan sulfate disaccharide unit): ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT): ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • Sodium (GAG fixed-charge counter-ion): ? unknown (not simulated)

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Glycogen (glycoCEST): search 'intervertebral disc glycogen content' returned only a tangential paper (PMID 41508214) about GSK3beta signaling, no actual glycogen store quantified. NP cells sparsely cellular, not documented as glycogen stores; absent from IVD CEST target list.; [model's own exclusion] 31P metabolite categories (PME, PDE, PCr, ATP resonances): excluded as 31P MRS peak groupings, not 1H CEST pools; and ATP/creatine pools are below 1 mM in this low-cellularity tissue.; [model's own exclusion] Lipid CH2: excluded as a 1H MRS spectral grouping of unrelated lipids, not a definable pool.; [model's own exclusion] Free glucose and free lactate in IVD interstitium: only numerical diffusion models found (PMID 39366140, 40651968, 30283342); no direct mM tissue measurement, and these are diffusional transients rather than stored pools. Not listed.; [model's own exclusion] Free hydroxyproline and free glycine in degenerate discs (PMID 16319755): degeneration breakdown products (not healthy-tissue homeostatic pools) and the HR-MAS paper reports relative peak intensities, not extracted mM values. Not listed.; [model's own exclusion] Pharmacological CEST probes (Iopromide in PMID 23818244): exogenous, excluded as non-endogenous.; [model's own exclusion] Aggrecan core protein and collagen as whole-molecule molarities: whole-molecule molarity is micromolar-range, below the 1 mM threshold; their CEST relevance is captured via the amide residue-equivalent APT pool and the GAG disaccharide-unit pool, both already listed.

Glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST; chondroitin/dermatan sulfate disaccharide unit) — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 150.00 mM typical (estimated ~50-300 mM in disaccharide-unit terms (healthy nucleus pulposus); declines with degeneration)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: No direct disaccharide-unit mM for IVD found; GAG reported in mg/g wet tissue (PMID 8157495) not mM. Estimate from: NP ~80% water; GAG a major dry-matrix component; disaccharide repeat unit MW ~360-380 g/mol with several exchangeable -OH/-NH and 1 fixed charge per unit; 30-50 mg GAG/g wet tissue NP converts to ~100-150 mM disaccharide units. Cross-checked against rabbit IVD Na+ counter-ion 269.7 mM (PMID 22543251) = fixed-charge density, same order. Midpoint ~150 mM. n_exchangeable_protons per disaccharide ~3.

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (sugar hydroxyl OH (alcoholic/sugar OH on both residues) [hydroxyl]: concentration 50-300 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.66-3.73%, 1.5 T: 1.39-7.44%, 3 T: 3.24-15.37%, 5 T: 6.13-25.64%, 7 T: 8.67-32.55%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • Per overlap diagnostics, at 0.5T the GAG amide (+3.5) is 0 Hz from the APT amide (+3.5) - a complete collision, so the amide cannot be separated from APT at any field (gap stays 0 Hz).
  • The GAG OH (+0.82) blurs with the APT amide at 0.5T (56.9 Hz gap < 137.7 Hz linewidth) and with the APT rNOE and MT pools
  • by 1.5-7T the OH separates from the amide, but it always sits only ~2.2 ppm from the enormous semisolid MT pool (-2.4 ppm), which has a ~16 kHz broadened line and is never resolved - the OH contrast is a shoulder on the MT/background, not a free peak. The hydroxyl-vs-amide within the molecule also overlap at low field.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 is small (0.25-1.0 µT) and direct_sat_bandwidth is only 10.6-42.6 Hz, well below the 0.82 ppm offset (17-43 Hz at 0.5-3T, 260 Hz at 7T). Direct saturation does not mask the OH offset except near 0.5T where the offset (~17 Hz) is comparable to the 10.6 Hz band. Literature confirms 3T gagCEST is degraded by direct saturation of the fast-exchanging OH (PMID 22213239), favoring low B1 and high field.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • The OH kex 600 s−1 was borrowed from myo-inositol (PMID 20951217, brain, 7T, origin of k not stated as phantom vs in vivo), and the OH shift came from GAG phantoms (PMID 30230599) and one in-vivo cartilage value (PMID 21460030). No intervertebral-disc-specific OH exchange rate exists in the table.
  • GAG is a charged, macromolecular, crowded matrix; in vivo kex for disc OH can differ from the small-solute inositol value by an order of magnitude, and the generic small-solute T1/T2 are wrong for a proteoglycan. This is the single largest source of uncertainty in the simulated contrast, which I treat as an upper bound.
  • The amide kex (65.5 s−1) is also class-level, borrowed from brain/liver, not disc.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 1.926% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Fast OH exchange (k~600 s−1) merged toward water peaks at low-to-moderate B1; the sweep optimum at 0.5 µT reflects the balance between exchange-driven transfer and direct-saturation loss, shifting up slightly with B0. Tsat ~750 ms is sufficient for the OH pool to reach quasi-steady transfer.
    recommended sequence: 3.979% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At 3T the 0.82 ppm offset is ~43 Hz, clearing the 31.9 Hz direct-sat band, so a modestly higher B1 (0.75 µT) is optimal; fast OH exchange still forbids high B1 (direct-sat domination). 1 s matches the 29748204 disc protocol.
    recommended sequence: 8.805% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Higher B0 separates the OH from water (686 Hz) and the direct-sat band is 42.6 Hz, so the optimum climbs to 1.0 µT before direct saturation erodes the fast-OH transfer. Contrast ~15.8% is an upper bound (see caveat).
    recommended sequence: 15.770% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=1500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — 7T gives the best OH/water separation (961 Hz); the sweep optimum stays at 1.0 µT with a longer 1.5 s to build the fast-exchange transfer and suppress MT contamination. This matches the 7T-preferred gagCEST conclusion of PMID 22213239.
    recommended sequence: 21.180% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note:

  • Literature gagCEST in the disc uses MTRasym at a single fixed B1 (0.8 µT, 1 s; PMID 29748204, 25758361), but MTRasym at ~0.8 ppm is heavily contaminated by semisolid MT and the APT/NOE pools, so the disc-specific studies that work (PMID 33475842) use multiparametric multi-pool Lorentzian/multi-pool Z-spectrum fitting, not raw MTRasym.
  • Because the OH is fast-exchanging and buried under MT, a multi-pool fit or AREX (which removes T1/direct-sat bias) is preferred over MTRasym; the swept low B1 is appropriate for the slow/intermediate regime. AREX is especially relevant at 3-7T for the OH.

Potential clinical impact

gagCEST (GAG -OH exchange, ~6-8 ppm): 7 CEST/NOE application and 2 metabolite-change studies verified (8 human, 1 animal; 137 humans, 0 animals; 7 dropped by verification). Strong CEST evidence: gagCEST (3T) applied in lumbar and cervical disc degeneration, spondyloarthritis, AIS, and a porcine pH model, all showing lower GAG signal with degeneration. GAG depletion confirmed by DMMB/dGEMRIC/IHC in human, rabbit, mouse, bovine, pig.

Caveats / critique (9 points, 427 words) — 150 mM is a per-disaccharide-unit figure; GAG FCD in nucleus pulposus is often quoted in mM FCD, so order-of-magnitude is plausible but not directly validated a…
  • 150 mM is a per-disaccharide-unit figure; GAG FCD in nucleus pulposus is often quoted in mM FCD, so order-of-magnitude is plausible but not directly validated against MRS. The real gagCEST literature (PMID 22253087, 25758361, 26583472) measures an OH-CEST effect that tracks FCD, not an amide signal, which is consistent with the hydroxyl pool dominating.
  • The 150 mM was simulated as a small-solute pool with generic T1/T2, but GAG is a macromolecule embedded in a proteoglycan matrix with very different T1/T2 and water mobility; this inflates/deflates contrast unpredictably.
  • The simulated ~8.8% at 3T far exceeds the ~2-3% MTRasym reported in vivo in healthy lumbar discs (PMID 25758361, 26583472), so the with-vs-without number is an upper bound and should not be read as the clinical MTRasym.
  • Amide class is correct for the N-acetyl -NHCOCH3 (one per disaccharide), but in practice gagCEST is dominated by the OH pool, so this amide is a minor, buried component. Hydroxyl class is correct and is the true gagCEST pool; 5 OH is a reasonable per-unit count.
  • The glycoNOE (rnoe) group was NOT SIMULATED because 13 protons was rejected as an invalid per-repeating-unit count and the rNOE effective rate is unknown - no contrast can be claimed for it. The carboxylate is correctly excluded. Neglected: no separate amide-vs-OH separation was attempted, and the two pools share the 3.5 ppm amide with APT.
  • In-vivo gagCEST (PMID 22253087, 25758361, 26583472) is quantified at the OH offset (~0.8-1 ppm, matching the simulated 0.825 ppm). The amide component is not resolved from APT in vivo because it shares ~3.5 ppm. No in-vivo measurement of a distinct GAG-amide shift was found; the 3.5 ppm is a class-level borrowed value. None major. OH and amide both captured.
  • The glycoNOE C-H upfield pool is present in the literature as a confound but is not a 1H-exchange pool and was not simulated. Groups not simulated: C-H (glycoNOE; ring C-H, N-acetyl CH3, CH2) [rnoe] -- not simulated: Glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST; chondroitin/dermatan sulfate disaccharide unit): n_exchangeable_protons=13 is not a per-molecule (or per-repeating-unit) proton count.
  • Use 1-12; for a polymer or macromolecular pool give the concentration PER repeating unit (e.g. glycogen ~250-300 mM glucosyl units x 3 hydroxyl protons; the mobile-protein amide pool ~200-300 mM x 1), not a whole-molecule count. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor
  • Primary gagCEST target for IVD; established real CEST pool (PMID 23818244). Multiple exchangeable -OH/-NH per disaccharide unit; pH-sensitive. Concentration declines with degeneration (PMID 28767620, 16319755).

Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 250.00 mM typical (estimated ~100-300 mM amide-proton-equivalent (one amide per amino-acid-residue equivalent unit))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: No direct amide-unit mM for IVD found; APT reported as relative Z-spectra contrast (PMID 33475842, 42286353) not absolute concentration. Reported per amino-acid-residue amide-equivalent unit (n_exchangeable_protons = 1 per amide). Estimate from typical soft-tissue mobile amide pool (~200-300 mM residue-equivalent in cellular tissues) adjusted for IVD low cellularity (<1% NP cells) but substantial extracellular collagen/aggrecan-core-protein amide. Collagen ~56% of endplate cartilage dry weight (PMID 24273192); each residue contributes one backbone amide. Net ~100-300 mM, midpoint ~250 mM.

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (backbone amide NH (N-H-C=O) [amide]: concentration 100-300 mM, kex 15-158 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.34-3.52%, 1.5 T: 0.81-7.87%, 3 T: 0.94-13.12%, 5 T: 1.12-15.24%, 7 T: 1.22-16.36%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • Per overlap diagnostics, the APT amide (+3.5 ppm) is in EXACT collision (0 Hz) with the GAG amide (+3.5 ppm) at every field strength - these two are inseparable by frequency; the simulation lumps them. At 0.5T the APT amide also blurs with the GAG OH (+0.82, 56.9 Hz < 137.7 Hz) and with the MT pool (-2.4).
  • The APT rNOE (-3.5) is well downfield of everything but shares the upfield region with the (un-simulated) GAG glycoNOE at ~-1 to -3.5 ppm, a potential low-field confound. The 3.5 ppm APT is the dominant downfield peak; the semisolid MT pool (-2.4) is never resolved from the APT rNOE (16 kHz linewidth).

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 0.5-0.75 µT with direct_sat_bandwidth 21.3-31.9 Hz. The 3.5 ppm amide offset is far from water (105 Hz at 3T, 297 Hz at 7T), so direct saturation never spills into the APT peak. The APT is well-separated from water at all fields (slow exchange, CEST-favorable per diagnostics). No direct-saturation masking of the amide.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • Both kex values are class-level and borrowed: the amide 65.5 s−1 from human brain/liver in vivo (PMID 40228056, 23008121), and the rNOE 5 s−1 from a protein phantom (PMID 25996515, not a disc).
  • The disc is a cold, acidic, high-ionic-strength, macromolecularly crowded environment; the mobile amide kex and especially the rNOE relayed-NOE transfer rate can differ in vivo in the disc from these values by a substantial factor. The generic small-solute T1/T2 are also wrong for the disc matrix.
  • These caveats lower confidence in the absolute simulated contrast, though the qualitative APT/NOE structure is robust and well established in the disc literature.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=1500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 2.456% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Slow-exchange backbone amide (k~65 s−1) is well-separated from water; the optimum is at low B1 (0.5 µT) to avoid direct-saturation of water, with long Tsat (3 s) to let the slow pool reach steady transfer. The peak sits low in B1 because slow exchange loses little to direct saturation until B1 is raised.
    recommended sequence: 5.675% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At 3T the APT offset (105 Hz) is clear of the 31.9 Hz direct-sat band, so the optimum rises to 0.75 µT. Slow exchange still favors the lower end of B1; 3 s Tsat matches the established disc APT protocol and is needed for the slow pool.
    recommended sequence: 7.725% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — 5T keeps the APT well clear of water (175 Hz) and the sweep optimum stays at 0.75 µT; the slow amide does not benefit from higher B1 because direct-saturation of water begins to dominate. Long Tsat retained for slow exchange.
    recommended sequence: 9.034% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — 7T maximizes APT/water separation (297 Hz) so the 0.75 µT optimum holds; contrast plateaus near 9.7% because the mobile amide pool is fixed and further B1 only adds direct saturation. 3 s Tsat is standard for slow-exchange APT at high field.
    recommended sequence: 9.725% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: The disc studies extract APT by multiparametric multi-pool Z-spectrum fitting (PMID 33475842) and by CEST-derived amide/NOE parameters (PMID 42286353), not by naive MTRasym, because the 3.5 ppm peak is contaminated by GAG-amide and the upfield NOE confounds MTRasym. Slow-exchange APT at ~65 s−1 with a 0.75 µT / 3 s optimum is well suited to AREX (removes T1/direct-sat bias) and to multi-pool Lorentzian fitting; simple MTRasym is insufficient because of the upfield NOE and the GAG-amide overlap.

Potential clinical impact

amide (APT, ~3.5 ppm): 0 CEST/NOE application and 1 metabolite-change studies verified (0 human, 1 animal; 0 humans, 0 animals; 3 dropped by verification). CEST evidence limited to chronic low back pain / painful-disc Z-spectrum studies at 3T, where APT is used as a pH surrogate (reduced in degenerate/sore discs). No non-CEST method directly quantified the mobile amide-protein pool itself; indirect acid/microenvironment evidence (lactic acid, intradiscal pH) supports where an APT signal could apply.

Caveats / critique (7 points, 349 words) — 250 mM mobile-protein/peptide amide is a generic soft-tissue APT concentration and is not disc-specific. The nucleus pulposus is dominated by type-II collagen a…
  • 250 mM mobile-protein/peptide amide is a generic soft-tissue APT concentration and is not disc-specific. The nucleus pulposus is dominated by type-II collagen and proteoglycan, with relatively little free mobile peptide; the annulus is dominated by type-I collagen (a macromolecular, semisolid pool that feeds MT, not the mobile APT). So 250 mM may overstate the mobile amide pool in the NP.
  • In the multiparametric disc studies (PMID 33475842, 42286353) APT is extracted as a separate fitted component and tracks pH, confirming the pool exists and is CEST-visible, but the concentration was not independently validated by MRS. The simulated ~7.7% at 3T is therefore an upper bound.
  • Backbone amide class is correct (one -NH per peptide bond, slow exchange, ~3.5 ppm, canonical APT). The aliphatic rNOE side-chain class is also correct and is the standard upfield NOE confound. The amide kex (65.5 s−1) and shift are class-level, borrowed from brain/liver in vivo - no disc-specific amide measurement exists.
  • The rNOE kex (5 s−1) is a class value from protein phantoms (PMID 25996515), not a disc measurement. Neglected: none major; the two pools (amide downfield, rNOE upfield) are the standard APT/NOE pair. The 3.5 ppm amide and -3.5 ppm rNOE are the canonical in-vivo APT/NOE offsets, consistent with the multiparametric disc Z-spectrum fits (PMID 33475842).
  • No disc-specific shift deviation from 3.5 ppm was found. The simulated amide shift (3.5) is identical to the GAG amide, so it cannot be separated from GAG-amide in vivo. None. Amide and rNOE captured. Side-chain amide/Asn-Gln amides and Arg/His would be minor and are folded into the mobile amide/rNOE pools.
  • no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Well-established IVD CEST target (APT used in chronic LBP studies). pH-sensitive; degeneration pH drops reduce APT amplitude.
  • Much IVD amide is semi-solid collagen (restricted exchange), so the freely-exchanging mobile fraction may sit at the lower end of the range. [Unsourced reasoning] 1 numeric step(s) rest on an unsourced assumption: 'Each amino-acid residue contributes one backbone amide; reporting unit'.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — Sagittal slab centred on the L3-L4 intervertebral disc at the midsagittal midline

Why this scan:

  • A sagittal lumbar slab at L3-L4 cuts through the intervertebral disc (nucleus pulposus and annulus fibrosus) plus vertebral body marrow, paraspinal muscle and subcutaneous fat in one FOV. GAG concentration is far highest in nucleus pulposus (dry-weight fraction ~0.62) and lower in AF, near- absent in marrow/fat, and measurable in muscle extracellular matrix.
  • The mobile-protein/amide pool is high in dense neural/muscle tissue and low in the avascular gel-like nucleus.
  • Because these two pools vary across ROIs in opposite ways, an ROI-contrast pattern at 3.5 ppm that tracks GAG (high NP, low fat) versus one tracking protein (high muscle/cord, low NP) separates a real gagCEST/amide effect from a generic MT/NOE background that would look similar across tissues at a given offset.
ROIWhere it is drawnRole
nucleus pulposus target tissueCentral gel region of the L3-L4 disc on the midsagittal plane, the inner ~40% of disc height/width, bounded by the annulus, drawn on the T2w reference image.Primary target tissue; highest GAG content (NP > AF); low cellularity so low mobile-protein/amide pool. Tabulated T1/T2/MT available.
annulus fibrosus target tissuePeripheral laminar region of the same L3-L4 disc, the outer ~30-40% band surrounding the nucleus, drawn on T2w.Disc sub-region with lower GAG than nucleus (AF ~0.43-0.52 vs NP ~0.62 dry-weight) and higher collagen/protein; internal concentration gradient for GAG. Tabulated parameters available.
vertebral body marrowPosterior portion of the L3 vertebral body just cephalad to the disc, fat-containing cancellous marrow, avoiding the cortical rim.Low-GAG / low-mobile-protein fat-dominant reference; MT/NOE-dominated background. Tabulated parameters available.
paraspinal muscleRight paraspinal (multifidus/iliocostalis) muscle belly posterior to the spinous processes at the L3-L4 level.High-mobile-protein/amide muscle with only low GAG in connective tissue; tests whether the 3.5 ppm signal tracks protein rather than GAG. Tabulated parameters available.
subcutaneous fatAnterior and posterior subcutaneous fat depot at the L3-L4 level, drawn in a region clear of muscle and skin.Null reference: negligible GAG and mobile protein; residual signal is pure MT/fat contamination, confirming B0/B1 behaviour. Tabulated parameters available.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed Gaussian (duty-cycled) train, B1=0.75 µT, 1500 pulses × 0.5 ms (interpulse delay 1.5 ms, duty cycle 25%), total Tsat=3000 ms, TR=12000 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model): 1500×0.5 ms = 750 ms of RF on time spread over 3000 ms (25% duty) with a TR of 12 s. Mean RF power over the whole cycle is low (short on-time, 25% duty, 0.75 µT), keeping specific absorption far under the 3 T body-tissue limit (~2 W/kg head/4 W/kg whole-body). Spine/back region has good coil efficiency and no critical-organ RF hotspot, so this is comfortably SAR-feasible.

Compromise rationale:

  • The physicist recommended 0.75 µT/1000 ms for GAG (gagCEST) and 0.75 µT/3000 ms for APT. Both share B1=0.75 µT, so B1 is not the compromise - the saturation time is.
  • I adopt B1=0.75 µT and extend Tsat to 3000 ms, which is APT-optimal and over-saturates GAG (GAG exchange is slow amide ~1-10/s so longer saturation only marginally increases its already-saturated pool, with little penalty).
  • The 25% duty cycle and TR=12 s cost recovered magnetization, lowering absolute contrast for both, but that is uniform across ROIs so the differential (concentration-tracking) contrast is preserved. This single protocol favours APT fully and GAG near-fully; neither is under-saturated at 3.5 ppm.

Fat suppression: SPIR (spectral inversion-recovery) prepulse. The slab contains the fat-rich L3 vertebral body marrow immediately adjacent to the disc and large anterior/posterior subcutaneous fat depots; without suppression these high-signal fat regions would dominate MTRasym at low offsets and spill into the disc/muscle ROIs via partial volume. SPIR is chosen over SPAIR for robustness across the inhomogeneous body-coil B1 over the spine-slab geometry.

Motion mitigation:

  • Spine: CSF pulsation is the main motion source at the canal level, and the lumbar disc itself is quasi-static.
  • Use a 2-shot average per offset and a short echo train; no respiratory gate is needed at the lumbar level (below the diaphragm), so no breath-hold constraint - this keeps the ~12 s TR x 8 offsets (~100 s plus WASSR) practical. Avoid the swallowing/gastric-motion zone by centring on L3-L4.
  • If a slight respiratory phase shift is seen at L5-S1 in some subjects, an optional navigator can be added, but it is not budgeted here.

Slice coverage: Sagittal slab, midsagittal midline, centred on the L3-L4 intervertebral disc. Slab thickness 40 mm (e.g. 10×4 mm or 8×5 mm) spanning from just above the L3 endplate to just below the L4 endplate, giving in-plane resolution ~1×1 x 4 mm so the nucleus (~10-12 mm) and AF band can be separately contoured. FOV ~280×220 mm to include the vertebral bodies, posterior paraspinal muscle and anterior/posterior subcutaneous fat.

Structures in FOV: nucleus pulposus, annulus fibrosus, vertebral body marrow, paraspinal muscle, subcutaneous fat, spinal cord / CSF (canal), vertebral cortical bone, endplate

Z-spectrum sampling offsets:

  • -8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference (no pool)
  • -3.50 ppm: APT rNOE aliphatic C-H (mobile protein upfield), gagCEST rNOE (glycoNOE, ~-1 ppm broad upfield)
  • -1.00 ppm: gagCEST glycoNOE / sugar rNOE pool negative offset
  • +0.00 ppm: water (0 ppm), symmetric reference
  • +1.00 ppm: sugar OH (gagCEST fast exchange ~0.8 ppm), WASSR-style B0 reference point
  • +2.00 ppm: intermediate CEST region, WASSR B0 reference point
  • +3.50 ppm: GAG N-acetyl amide NH (gagCEST), mobile protein/peptide backbone amide (APT)
  • +8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference (no pool)

Differential analysis plan:

  • For each ROI, fit a Lorentzian difference curve (Lorentzian-difference CEST, LD-CEST) and compute MTRasym at +3.5 ppm (and its mirror at -3.5 ppm) with WASSR B0 correction, then compare the 3.5 ppm MTRasym across ROIs.
  • GAG confirmation: a 3.5 ppm contrast that is highest in nucleus pulposus > annulus fibrosus >> muscle > marrow > fat (tracking the GAG dry-weight gradient) while the -3.5 ppm rNOE and 0 ppm stay flat argues for a genuine gagCEST contribution.
  • APT confirmation: a 3.5 ppm contrast highest in paraspinal muscle (and AF) > nucleus, with a corresponding elevated -3.5 ppm aliphatic rNOE, argues for a protein/amide origin. If the 3.5 ppm signal is similar in all ROIs (flat across NP, AF, muscle, marrow, fat), it is generic MT/NOE background, not a metabolite.
  • A mixed pattern (high in both muscle and nucleus with low fat) indicates both pools contribute. Report per-ROI MTRasym and the ROI-to-ROI rank correlation against the assumed GAG and protein concentration vectors.

Not actively targeted: Sodium (GAG fixed-charge counter-ion) was not actively targeted: it is not an exchangeable CEST pool and the prior physicist agent gave it no detectable simulated CEST contrast at any field strength; it is also outside the budget of this single-compromise saturation scheme. It is excluded from organ_predictions.

Caveats:

  • Key limits for this anatomy: (1) Partial volume - the nucleus is small (~10-12 mm) and the AF is a thin band, so 1×1x4 mm in-plane resolution still mixes NP/AF, and bone-cortex partial volume at the disc margin corrupts the disc ROIs.
  • (2) B0/B1 inhomogeneity across the spine slab from the body coil (bone-air and marrow-fat susceptibility) means WASSR correction is essential and B1-scaling (0.7x/1.3x) shows how much contrast survives. (3) A single 0.75 µT/3000 ms / 25% duty protocol is APT-optimal but cannot simultaneously optimise GAG exchange.
  • (4) GAG and amide both sit at 3.5 ppm, so they are not separated by a single offset; only the ROI-contrast pattern across tissues disentangles them. (5) Marrow, muscle, and fat concentration values used here are reasoned estimates with high uncertainty, not directly measured. (6) CSF pulsation and any respiration at L5-S1 can shift the slice-to-anatomy relationship between offsets.
